Title: Hyperonirism: 'I feel like my brain never stops at night'
Subhead: 'Strange nights' (4/7). This little-known phenomenon is characterized by intense, continuous dreams, non-restorative sleep and daytime fatigue. It was first described by two American doctors in 1995.

Title: Free the knees! A plea for shorts at the office
Subhead: While no law prohibits it, wearing shorts to work is often enough to have you pegged as a professional slacker. Could this laid-back dress code actually be a form of environmental avant-gardism instead? Le Monde's Nicolas Santolaria explores the question in his column.

Subhead: 'The Golden Owl's last secrets' (1/6). Thirty-one years after it was buried, the treasure known as La Chouette d'Or, or Golden Owl, was discovered on the night of October 2, 2024. Yet, many 'chouetteurs' – the name given to the community of treasure hunters obsessed with this elusive statuette – never stopped searching for 'the real one.' Something doesn't add up.

Title: Cape Verde offers fragile refuge for persecuted gay Africans: 'It's like I'm a prisoner in paradise'
Subhead: The most LGBTQ+ tolerant country in Africa, according to a survey by Afrobarometer, the archipelago has become home to many Africans fleeing repression tied to their sexual orientation. However, the lack of an asylum policy has prevented them from obtaining residency permits.

Title: In Barcelona, Russian and Ukrainian exiles cross paths at the baths: 'We don't talk about the war, not even at the banya'
Subhead: For the past year, traditional steam baths from Eastern Europe and Russia have been springing up across the Catalan capital. Popular with both Russians and Ukrainians – who arrived by the thousands on the Costa Brava at the start of the war in 2022 – the establishments have become an unexpected place for the two communities to coexist.
